title: AI isn't replacing your job. It's turning it into low-paid gig work
lede: A Rest of World essay argues AI training platforms are turning skilled professions into piecework, paying well to recruit experts and then cutting rates and moving on.

points: Scale AI's Outlier advertises up to $180 an hour for US physicians, against up to $7.50 an hour for Tagalog work in the Philippines.
The author spent six years interviewing Venezuelan data labelers, including a family whose best day earned $20 before the task vanished.
Remotasks left Venezuela in 2021 and Kenya, Nigeria and Pakistan in 2024, citing security changes.
Platform terms allow withholding pay and closing accounts without notice; laid-off lawyers and scientists describe rates falling as projects run on.
Lawsuits against Scale AI and Mercor are testing whether these workers have been misclassified.

points.text: Commenters split on whether this is ordinary industrialization; one reply says AI has handed them bigger tasks, not smaller ones.
Several call for unions as the only real counterweight to platforms setting pay on their own terms.
One argues software work was pushed toward underpaid labor by wage suppression long before AI arrived.
Others expect gig work to be a stop on the way to the jobs disappearing entirely.
